rules.title: Exits from a floor area: number, separation, travel distance, dead-end corridors (BC Building Code 2024, Part 3)
rules.jurisdiction: Province of BC; City of Vancouver (Vancouver Building By-law 2025 follows these clauses)

source.title: BC Building Code 2024, Division B, Part 3 (Safety within floor areas; Exits)
source.section: Div B 3.4.2.1 (minimum number of exits: two, unless the floor area is not more than 150 m² and the occupant load not more than 60); 3.4.2.3 (least distance between two required exits: one half the maximum overall diagonal dimension of the floor area, but need not be more than 9 m for a sprinklered floor area or one with a public corridor); 3.4.2.4 and 3.4.2.5 (travel distance, measured from a suite door to the nearest exit where suites open on a public corridor; 45 m in a sprinklered floor area, 30 m otherwise, residential occupancy); 3.3.1.9 (dead-end corridors not more than 6 m long); 3.1.17.1 (occupant load of a dwelling unit: two persons per sleeping room)
source.verify: The figures and clause numbers were entered from recollection of the NBC 2020 / BCBC 2024 clauses (3.4.2.1, 3.4.2.3, 3.4.2.4, 3.4.2.5, 3.3.1.9, 3.1.17.1), not read from the code text, and must be confirmed against it; in particular the exact wording of 3.4.2.3 (the 9 m cap is quoted as applying to a sprinklered floor area), the sentence of 3.3.1.9 that sets the 6 m dead end, the in-force date of BCBC 2024 (entered as 10 March 2025), and the Province's single-exit-stair provisions for residential buildings up to six storeys, which this rule does not model.
